title: POC scoping - workload modeling for Horizon Finance
next_steps: Provide workload sample logs for modeling
action_items: Samira Patel: Send POC proposal and pricing (due 2027-08-13)
Priya Nair: Draft benchmark test plan and resource estimate (due 2027-08-18)
Alex Moreno: Share production traffic sample and token histograms (due 2027-08-16)
Morgan Lee: Confirm VPC peering requirements and firewall rules (due 2027-08-20)
summary: POC scoping call to capture Horizon Finance production workload for a 6-week POC. Primary goals: validate latency and cost targets under peak QPS, measure concurrency behavior with gpt-like models, and compare hosted vs dedicated deployment for throughput predictability. Security and VPC peering are blockers before benchmark runs.
transcript:
00:00:04 - Samira (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Samira from Redwood. quick roll call?
00:00:10 - Alex (CTO): Alex here, CTO, horizon finance. Morgan on audio, jenna joining in a sec.
00:00:18 - Morgan (SRE): Morgan - SRE.
00:00:22 - Jenna (Head of Data): Jenna - head of data, sorry i'm a minute late.
00:00:26 - Priya (SE): Priya from Redwood, i'm the solutions engineer, i'll lead the benchmark planning.
00:00:33 - Samira: Great, agenda — confirm success criteria, capture qps/concurrency and token distributions, agree benchmark timeline, identify security blockers.
00:00:47 - Alex: Sounds good. Our main ask is to see if we can serve our fraud-detection summary feature at 150 QPS peak, 60 concurrent model contexts, 95th pct latency < 500ms and cost target <$0.003 per 1k tokens. is that realistic?
00:01:10 - Priya: ok, good concrete targets. couple of clarifying q's — when you say 150 QPS is that steady or burst? what's the arrival pattern?
00:01:22 - Alex: it's bursty — steady at 20 qps, bursts up to 150 for 30-90s, maybe 3-4 times per hour during market open.
00:01:36 - Morgan: concurrency wise, each request spins up up to 3 internal calls, so effective concurrency can spike. also we have long prompts — average input tokens ~800, output ~120 tokens.
00:01:50 - Priya: got it, long inputs with short outputs. that's helpful — that affects GPU memory and kv-cache behavior.
00:02:02 - Samira: for the poc we usually ask for a 4-week run: week 0 instrumentation + dataset handoff, week 1 small-scale smoke tests, week 2 full benchmarks, week 3 analysis and decision. does that align with your timeline?
00:02:19 - Alex: timeline ok but we need benchmark results before our Sept 15 platform review — so start by Aug 23 latest.
00:02:29 - Priya: we'll target Aug 23 for the benchmark window. can you share production traffic samples (timestamps, token counts per request, qps by minute)?
00:02:42 - Jenna: yes we'll extract one week of traffic and token histograms. expect a lot of variability — some requests are >2k tokens.
00:02:56 - Morgan: security question — can the Redwood dedicated option sit in our VPC with peering and customer-managed KMS? we need SOC2 + audit logs.
00:03:07 - Samira: yes dedicated supports VPC peering and customer KMS/HSM; we will provide SOC2 docs and the audit log retention options.
00:03:19 - Alex: good. another constraint — we need deterministic fallbacks, i.e., if dedicated capacity is saturated we want automatic fallback to a lower-cost hosted model variant without exposing PII.
00:03:33 - Priya: we can route by policy and set automatic fallback to a quantized model variant; we'll include masking and prompt redaction steps during the benchmark.
00:03:45 - Jenna: what's your suggested benchmark harness and metrics? we care about p95 latency, p99 tail, throughput at target concurrency, GPU utilization, and token cost breakdown.
00:03:58 - Priya: plan: replay sampled requests at scaled QPS, run steady-state ramps for 15m then bursts matching your pattern; measure latency distributions, memory/KV hit rates, and token-level cost. we'll also try batching and caching toggles to measure unit cost impact.
00:04:17 - Alex: do you support running with our exact model weights or only Redwood-curated models?
00:04:24 - Samira: both — for dedicated/private we can bring-your-own-model; for hosted we recommend the verified variants. for POC we can do a BYOM trial if you can provide the weights and license.
00:04:36 - Morgan: licensing is fine. network — we'll want an IP allowlist and specific egress controls, also can we limit logging for PII redaction?
00:04:47 - Priya: yes, we can configure log redaction and provide options for token-level pseudonymization during processing.
00:04:56 - Alex: can you ballpark resources? e.g., to hit 150 QPS with 800 token inputs and streaming outputs, how many GPU cards?
00:05:07 - Priya: rough estimate depends on model size / quantization; for 7B quantized model maybe 4-8 A100-equivalent GPUs with batching; for 70B you would need 12-24; but since you have long inputs kv-cache will increase memory; we'll run profiling to refine.
00:05:24 - Samira: cost wise we need to model per-token cost; we'll provide a price sheet for hosted and an estimated bill for dedicated sizing after profiling.
00:05:34 - Jenna: token distribution — we'll share histograms, but typical: 60% requests <500 tokens, 30% between 500-1500, 10% >1500. output distribution: 85% under 200 tokens, 15% 200-800.
00:05:52 - Priya: that's great, it suggests caching short prefixes will help. also batching benefits depend on request latency SLO because batching adds some queuing delay.
00:06:05 - Alex: for success criteria: if p95 < 500ms and cost under target across our traffic profile we consider it a win. also want to validate canary deploy procedures and rollback.
00:06:18 - Priya: we'll include canary/rollback tests, A/B traffic split and verification checks.
00:06:27 - Morgan: what does the data flow look like during benchmarks — do we forward raw requests to Redwood or anonymize locally?
00:06:35 - Samira: during POC we prefer sample sanitized data. if you must send raw we can sign an NDA and use private deployment with customer-managed keys.
00:06:46 - Jenna: we'll send sanitized samples first.
00:06:49 - Samira: ok next — mechanicals: what endpoints do you hit? REST or streaming websockets?
00:06:55 - Alex: currently REST for synchronous calls and we use a small streaming websocket endpoint for long transcripts but won't use streaming for the fraud summary path yet.
00:07:06 - Priya: in that case we'll run both sync and simulated streaming to measure tail latency differences.
00:07:12 - Samira: any regulatory constraints or data residency?
00:07:16 - Alex: US-only data, and logs must be retained for 90 days, with audit logs exported to our SIEM.
00:07:24 - Priya: Redwood can export logs via S3 and forward to SIEM; we'll document retention and access controls.
00:07:31 - Alex: ok good.
00:07:34 - [00:21:03 - transcript jump — mid-call dive into technical profiling]
00:21:10 - Priya: diving deeper on concurrency — you mentioned each request fan-outs to 3 internal calls; is that sequential or parallel?
:21:18 - Morgan: it's parallel, but we join results before returning, so effective token throughput multiplies.
00:21:25 - Priya: that matters — if you fan-out 3x at 150 qps that's 450 model invocations per second peak. caching prefix across those calls could reduce token work if they share context.
00:21:39 - Jenna: many requests share a stable 200-token prefix (customer metadata); rest is dynamic.
00:21:46 - Priya: good candidate for prefix caching/KV reuse.
00:22:00 - Samira: for benchmarks we'll want two passes: (1) naive run with no caching/batching to get worst-case latencies, (2) optimized run with caching and batching heuristics.
00:22:12 - Alex: that helps demonstrate upside.
00:22:17 - Priya: we'll also instrument per-token cost, gpu util, and KV hit-rates; can you provide a test harness or should we replay via our load generator?
00:22:28 - Morgan: we'll export request logs; prefer you run generating traffic from your side to avoid exposing internal network, but we can peer and you can run in our VPC for fidelity.
00:22:40 - Samira: we'll propose both options in the POC doc.
00:22:43 - [00:38:05 - latency vs cost tradeoff conversation continued]
00:38:12 - Priya: small note — small batching windows reduce cost but might increase p95; we'll include an economic curve showing latency vs token cost for batching sizes.
00:38:25 - Jenna: perfect — that's exactly what finance will want to see.
00:38:30 - Alex: one more — can Redwood run synthetic stress tests for p99 tails? we care about tail latency under GC / kernel context swaps.
00:38:38 - Priya: yes, we'll instrument tail scenarios and include controlled GC/eviction events to see degradation and fallback behavior.
00:38:48 - Morgan: and capture metrics for rollback triggers.
00:38:51 - Samira: we'll add automated alert thresholds in the runbook.
00:39:00 - [00:50:00 - wrap-up and next steps]
00:50:04 - Samira: recap — we need: horizon to share one week of sanitized traffic + token histograms (alex/jenn a); Redwood to send POC proposal, security docs, and benchmark plan (samira/priya); target benchmark window week of Aug 23.
00:50:21 - Alex: confirmed.
00:50:24 - Morgan: will provide VPC peering details and firewall rules.
00:50:28 - Jenna: i'll share the traffic export by Aug 16.
00:50:32 - Priya: i'll send the benchmark test plan by Aug 18.
00:50:36 - Samira: i'll send pricing and POC agreement by EOD Aug 13.
00:50:41 - Alex: thanks all.
00:50:44 - Samira: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark kick-off. bye.
00:50:49 - [call ended]
